newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias Milling gets moratorium on debt.
newsitem.headline: Victorias Milling gets moratorium on debt.

text.p: Victorias Milling Company of the Philippines on Thursday secured a moratorium from bankers on debts amounting to 4.4 billion pesos ($167 million), company officials said.
The company is the biggest sugar miller in the Philippines.
"The banks have agreed to give the company breathing space," a Victorias Milling official who did not want to be named said.

The loans were taken from 32 banks, including Australia New Zealand Bank, Deutsche Bank, Philippine National Bank, Metropolitan Bank, Bank of the Philippine Islands, Land Bank of the Philippines and Banco National de Paris, the official said.
He said the banks had agreed on a moratorium on the principal repayments.
The official attributed the company's troubles to a steep fall in Philippine sugar prices.
"The banks agreed to continue supporting Victorias in its effort to maintain its leadership in the sugar industry," the official said.

The Asian Wall Street Journal in a report on Thursday said: "Market talk is that Victorias is struggling under several billion pesos of debt and that several listed banks have large exposures to the sugar miller."
